topic: nvidia dlss 5 coming to rtx remix for older games
headline_marked: NVIDIA's DLSS 5 [[comes to RTX Remix]] to 'enhance' older games
headline: NVIDIA's DLSS 5 comes to RTX Remix to 'enhance' older games
summary: NVIDIA's controversial DLSS 5 technology is now integrated into the RTX Remix modding platform, allowing users to inject AI-powered graphics enhancements into older PC titles.
details: NVIDIA's RTX Remix tool, available since early 2024, enables users to add ray tracing and AI-upscaled textures to older games. DLSS 5 is being added to this platform on October 23, following its integration into RTX Spark on October 16.

The technology, which significantly alters in-game character lighting, will also be officially added to Hogwarts Legacy on November 5. Early demonstrations suggest DLSS 5's visual impact has been toned down compared to its initial reveal.

However, the integration of DLSS 5 into RTX Remix and RTX Spark is met with controversy. Unlike previous DLSS versions, it negatively impacts frame rates rather than boosting them, a significant concern for many gamers.

Despite the official rollout, modders have already found ways to inject DLSS 5 into nearly any PC game using community-built applications like DLSS 5 Manager and DLSS 5 Swapper, provided the user has an NVIDIA RTX GPU.

These tools allow for the insertion of advanced lighting techniques into Vulkan and DirectX titles. The process is reportedly straightforward, with the software automatically detecting the correct rendering API and installing necessary files.

A word of caution: DLSS 5 mods may not function correctly with games that employ anti-cheat software, as seen in attempts to mod GTA V: Enhanced Edition. This issue is expected to diminish as NVIDIA officially supports DLSS 5 in more titles.

The primary criticism against DLSS 5 is that it compromises the artistic integrity of games, drastically altering lighting and character appearances. This, coupled with a significant performance hit, has led to widespread user dissatisfaction.

topic: canva announces layoffs and significant changes
headline_marked: Canva lays off [[1,271 employees]], impacting 22% of its staff
headline: Canva lays off 1,271 employees, impacting 22% of its staff
summary: The design platform is restructuring its teams and consolidating roles, with Sydney becoming a primary hub for product development.
details: Canva CEO Melanie Perkins announced significant organizational changes today, affecting 1,271 employees, which amounts to 22% of the company's workforce. Some employees will see changes to their roles, be asked to relocate, or will be laid off.

Perkins stated that these changes are necessary to "refound Canva" and prepare for the next decade by returning to smaller, empowered teams focused on community needs. The restructuring aims to simplify layers and consolidate overlapping responsibilities.

The company is merging its Product, Growth, and Platform teams into a single product organization. Sydney is designated as the primary home for more product teams and specialized roles requiring close collaboration.

Starting in January, Canva will also require most hybrid employees to work in the office 2 to 3 days per week, depending on their specific area. This move aims to foster better collaboration and context sharing.
Employees departing Canva will receive comprehensive benefits, including at least six months of salary, twelve months of healthcare coverage, and access to career support resources.
